lead.summary: Follow the day’s news live. Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Coalition says main focus of tobacco excise cut is tackling organised crime Anne Ruston , the shadow minister for health and aged care, spoke this morning to tout the Coalition’s plans to slash the tobacco excise by 80%, saying the effort is designed to “break the business model” of organised crime. This is very much designed to try and get the government back in control of the nicotine market, not organised crime gangs. … We are hoping that the combined package of what we’re proposing here, not just the dropping of the excise, but the regulation of the market and making it certainly more difficult for children to access these products. In the enforcement surge and the anti-smoking and anti-vaping campaigns, we are hoping to put downward pressure on smoking rates. Continue reading...

latest.summary: The latest updates from Flushing Meadows on day five You can mail Katy and follow us on TikTok and Bluesky It feels rather odd saying this, given that Osaka is a two-time former US Open champion, but she’s something of a wildcard contender this fortnight, having not won a title since 2021. But over the past year she’s been building momentum, after returning from her maternity leave in 2024, and there were plenty of green shoots on the grass at Wimbledon, where she beat Aryna Sabalenka en route to the quarter-finals. And Osaka has started strongly today, leading Siniakova 3-1 and serving at 40-15. Make that game, as the 13th seed’s pace is too much for the Czech to handle. Swiatek is serving for the first set at 5-3. And on her second set point, at her advantage, she takes it , when Podoroska prods a return wide. After starting with three holds to love, the set got closer, but the eighth seed found a way through and she’s skipping to the back of the court to start the second set. She looks up for this – and most importantly, more confident than she has done for so much of this year. Continue reading...
